description: 10 educational paragraphs across AI, NLP, Databases, OS, and Networks with human-annotated ground-truth named entities and formal definitions.

samples.text: Artificial Intelligence is defined as the branch of computer science focused on building systems capable of human-like reasoning. Alan Turing proposed the Turing Test in 1950 at the University of Manchester.

reference_definitions.definition: the branch of computer science focused on building systems capable of human-like reasoning

samples.text: Information Theory refers to the mathematical study of quantifying, storing, and communicating digital data. Claude Shannon published its foundational paper at Bell Labs in 1948.

reference_definitions.definition: the mathematical study of quantifying, storing, and communicating digital data

samples.text: Supervised learning means training a predictive function from labeled input-output examples. Researchers at Stanford University and Google widely apply supervised models to speech and vision tasks.

reference_definitions.definition: training a predictive function from labeled input-output examples

samples.text: Backpropagation is known as the standard algorithm for computing neural network gradients via the chain rule. Geoffrey Hinton and colleagues at the University of Toronto popularized deep representation learning.

reference_definitions.definition: the standard algorithm for computing neural network gradients via the chain rule

samples.text: Lemmatization is the process of reducing inflected words to their canonical dictionary base form. The WordNet lexical database was developed at Princeton University starting in 1985.

reference_definitions.definition: the process of reducing inflected words to their canonical dictionary base form

samples.text: The relational model is defined as a database abstraction organizing records into mathematical relations or tables. Edgar Codd introduced this framework while working at IBM in 1970.

reference_definitions.definition: a database abstraction organizing records into mathematical relations or tables

samples.text: Virtual memory refers to an operating system mechanism that maps isolated virtual addresses onto physical RAM frames. Multics and Unix pioneered early virtual memory designs at MIT in the 1960s.

reference_definitions.definition: an operating system mechanism that maps isolated virtual addresses onto physical RAM frames

samples.text: Hypertext Transfer Protocol is an application-layer standard for transmitting web resources across networks. Tim Berners-Lee created the World Wide Web at CERN in 1989.

reference_definitions.definition: an application-layer standard for transmitting web resources across networks

samples.text: Tokenization represents the segmentation of raw character streams into discrete sentences or words. Modern open-source pipelines in Python rely on libraries maintained by Explosion and Microsoft.

reference_definitions.definition: the segmentation of raw character streams into discrete sentences or words

samples.text: Public-key cryptography means using mathematically linked public and private keys for secure communication. Whitfield Diffie and Martin Hellman published key exchange principles in 1976, followed by RSA at MIT in 1977.

reference_definitions.definition: using mathematically linked public and private keys for secure communication
